newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian nun says Albanian town out of medicines.
newsitem.headline: Italian nun says Albanian town out of medicines.

text.p: An Italian nun in the troubled southern Albanian port of Vlore said on Thursday that a hospital there had been looted during the night and that no medicines were left to treat the sick and wounded.

"We have an urgent need of medicines for our clinic and for the hospital in Vlore that was attacked last night," the Italian news agency ANSA quoted the nun, who was not identified, as saying in a telephone interview.
"They have taken everything away and we don't know how we are going to treat the burns and gunshot wounds."
ANSA quoted the woman as saying that the Albanian army had cut off the town, which lies across the Adriatic from the small southern Italian port of Otranto.

"We don't know how to get hold of any medicines, maybe from Otranto by motorboat but we don't know how to pay for them," said the nun said, adding that some people had died on Wednesday night and the situation was likely to get worse.
Insurgents in several southern towns looted police and army weapons depots over the weekend.
Undeterred by a state of emergency and shoot-on-sight orders for security forces, the insurgents hold sway in Vlore, the Adriatic coastal town of Sarande and several other points.

Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Thursday that Italy was willing to supply humanitarian relief to Albania but that future structured economic aid from abroad would depend on a political solution being achieved to the country's crisis.
